title: Best Cozi Alternatives (2026)
description: Cozi's free tier now caps the calendar view and shows ads. Here are alternatives ranked on what's genuinely free forever, plus who should stick with Cozi.
directAnswer: People search for a Cozi alternative when the free tier that used to feel complete starts to feel like a trial: reviewers describe a 30-day calendar view limit, ads, and login or widget failures on an app some have used for ten years. The strongest alternatives are apps whose free tier is not a time-limited preview of the real product. Cozi's own reviewers also credit it with a decade of quiet reliability before this shift, which is worth weighing before switching. Kinrows is one newer, broader alternative, though it is iPhone-only and launches September 2026.
keyTakeaway: Cozi's paywall has crept onto features that used to feel free; the strongest alternatives don't time-limit the free tier at all.

sections.heading: Why people search for a Cozi alternative
sections.html:
Cozi is the best-known free family calendar and list app, and for years it earned real loyalty: "I have used this app for probably 10 years" — an App Store reviewer, 2★, "Used to be great," App Store US, 2026-07-31. That loyalty is what makes the recent complaints land hard. Reviewers describe the free tier narrowing: "Charges you to plan 30 days in advance" — an App Store reviewer, 1★, "Bad," App Store US, 2026-08-16. Others cite a steep subscription: "I was really disappointed with this app. Even after paying for the Gold subscription at $30/yr, most features were still locked and only available at the $80/yr subscription" — an App Store reviewer, 2★, "Requires $80/yr subscription to use," App Store US, 2026-08-24.

Technical friction compounds it: "The widget always says I'm signed out even though I'm not" — an App Store reviewer, 1★, "Widget Doesn't Work," App Store US, 2026-08-09. And a growing AI push is unwelcome to long-tenure users: "It seems like all the update are pushing more AI into this app" — an App Store reviewer, 2★, "Too many changes," App Store US, 2026-09-11.

sections.heading: What Cozi does well (ten-year loyalty is real)
sections.html: Cozi's core product — a shared calendar with per-person color coding and grocery/to-do lists — is simple enough that whole families, including multi-generational households, still rely on it daily. Reviewers who have used it for six or ten years are describing a genuinely dependable default, not a fad. Its meal planner and recipe box add real value on top of scheduling. Anyone frustrated by the newer paywalls and ads is reacting to recent changes layered on a product that, at its base, still works as advertised for a lot of households.

sections.heading: Ranked alternatives
sections.html:
The complaints driving people away from Cozi are about the free tier narrowing over time — a calendar view cap, ads, a subscription that used to feel optional. So this ranking weighs, in order: whether the core features stay free with no time limit, whether the app is ad-free without paying, and how broad the free feature set is beyond a calendar and a list.

  • TimeTree. Free and ad-supported (ad removal is paid), with useful per-event chat. A concentrated group of its own reviewers are currently leaving over AI features that reportedly train on calendar data even after opting out — worth knowing before you land there instead.
  • FamilyWall. A broader free-first hub (calendar, tasks, photos, location, finance) praised for elder-care coordination, but its own reviewers report frequent crashes after updates and broken invite flows that block new members from joining.
  • Skylight Calendar. An always-on physical wall display, not a phone app, so it solves a different problem: ambient visibility without ads or a login. It costs $170–$630 in hardware plus an optional roughly $79-a-year subscription for meal planning and chore rewards.
  • Maple. An AI-forward family organizer with an email-to-task assistant and chore tracker. Its own users report the same pattern driving people off Cozi: "recent updates introducing subscription models for previously free features" (paraphrased via aggregated user reports).
  • Kinrows. A free-core household organizer covering calendar, lists, budget, pantry, chores, trips and more, with no ads, no data sale, and no time-limited calendar view; only the optional AI Concierge is paid. It is iPhone-only and launches September 2026, so it is not an option today or for a mixed-OS household.

sections.heading: Who should stay with Cozi
sections.html: If your household has used Cozi for years without hitting the 30-day view cap or minding the ads, and the current feature set still covers what you need, switching costs more than it saves. Cozi's cross-platform reach (iOS, Android, web), meal planner, and long track record are real strengths that a newer app has to earn from zero. Cozi Gold is listed at $39 on Cozi's own site (cozi.com/cozi-gold, checked 2026-09-15), though the page does not state whether that is a monthly or yearly price — a reviewer separately cited $80 a year, possibly an older or bundled tier — so confirm the current terms at checkout before assuming either figure.

productFit.heading: A free core that isn't a time-limited preview
productFit.html: The complaint that drives most Cozi switching is a free tier that keeps shrinking — a 30-day calendar cap, ads, features that used to feel included. Kinrows takes a structurally different approach: the calendar, lists, pantry, budget, chores, trips and the rest of the free core app have no view limits, no ads, and no data sale, for the whole household, indefinitely. The only paid layer is the optional AI Concierge shown here — a daily brief and a chat that can actually move tasks, edit lists and log expenses — and it is a separate subscription you choose to add, not something the free app narrows around.

faq.a: Cozi's own site lists Cozi Gold at $39, though the page does not state whether that is a monthly or yearly price (cozi.com/cozi-gold, checked 2026-09-15). An App Store reviewer separately cited an $80-a-year figure, possibly an older or bundled tier; check the exact current terms at checkout. Gold removes ads, unlocks month view and calendar search on mobile, adds up to three reminders per event, and adds a birthday tracker and shopping mode. Whether it's worth it depends on how much the free tier's 30-day view cap and ads bother you.

faq.q: Why does Cozi look different on Android than iPhone?
faq.a: One reviewer described Cozi as looking "great on apple, terrible on pixel" (2★, App Store US, 2026-08-24), suggesting the iOS and Android apps do not currently match in design or reliability. This isn't a gap Kinrows can close either, since Kinrows is iPhone-only with no Android app; a mixed-OS household bothered by this specific complaint should look for a cross-platform app built to the same standard on both operating systems.

faq.q: What's a free alternative to Cozi?
faq.a: Kinrows' core app — calendar, lists, budget, pantry, chores and more — is free for the entire household with no ads and no time-limited calendar view, funded by a separate, optional Concierge AI subscription. TimeTree and Google Calendar's sharing feature are also free (TimeTree's free tier shows ads; Google Calendar's does not). Kinrows is iPhone-only and does not launch until September 2026.

faq.q: Why did Cozi start pushing AI features?
faq.a: A cluster of long-tenure Cozi reviewers say recent updates keep adding AI features they did not ask for: "It seems like all the update are pushing more AI into this app" (2★, App Store US, 2026-09-11). Cozi has not published a specific rationale that this page could verify. Kinrows takes the opposite approach: its AI Concierge is a separate, optional, paid add-on never bundled into the free core experience, so using the free app never means encountering AI features you didn't choose.
